vendors.name: Cribl Stream
vendors.offering: Telemetry pipeline to filter, reduce, enrich and route logs before SIEM
vendors.pricing: Cribl.Cloud free up to 1 TB/day; paid Stream ingest credits ~$0.27/GB (Standard, up to 5 TB/day) to $0.32/GB (Enterprise), $1 per credit, plus worker infrastructure

vendors.name: DataBahn
vendors.offering: Security data pipeline; vendor-reported claims of up to 60% lower SIEM ingestion costs (Microsoft Sentinel integration) and 40-50% telemetry reduction

vendors.name: Tenzir
vendors.offering: Security-focused pipeline engine (TQL) for SIEM, cloud and data cost optimization
vendors.pricing: Open-source edition free; commercial editions not public

vendors.name: Edge Delta Security Data Pipelines
vendors.offering: Edge-processed security pipelines with silent-source detection

vendors.name: Monad
vendors.offering: Security data ingestion and pipeline platform
vendors.pricing: not public on vendor site (AWS Marketplace listings exist, tier figures unverified)

vendors.name: Observo AI (SentinelOne)
vendors.offering: AI-native telemetry pipeline to enrich, summarize and route data; acquired by SentinelOne

vendors.name: Onum (CrowdStrike)
vendors.offering: Real-time telemetry pipeline feeding Falcon Next-Gen SIEM; acquired by CrowdStrike

vendors.name: Splunk Edge Processor
vendors.offering: Filter, mask, transform and route data before Splunk indexing
vendors.pricing: Included with Splunk Cloud Platform at no additional cost

paid_market_gaps.gap: Cribl's volume-based pricing draws reviewer complaints (costly as data volume scales; 'charges for everything it sees rather than everything it processes'); a reviewer asks for pricing options based on enterprise size or data volume
Pipeline tools need data-engineering effort to build and maintain; fit large SOCs, not small teams
Most security pipeline vendors publish no pricing; contact-sales only, blocking self-serve small-team buyers
Independent pipelines being absorbed by SIEM/XDR vendors, reducing vendor-neutral options

wtp_evidence: Enterprises pay per-GB pipeline fees (Cribl.Cloud ~$0.27-0.32/GB in credits above a free tier of up to 1 TB/day) to cut SIEM bills, and SIEM/XDR vendors buy pipeline startups (e.g. CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Onum); but PeerSpot reviewers call Cribl costly as volume scales and ask for pricing tiers by enterprise size or data volume (one small-scale user finds pricing good), and the generous free tier caps what small teams would pay.
bundling_note: SIEM vendors bundle or buy pipelines: Splunk Edge Processor is free with Splunk Cloud, CrowdStrike bought Onum, SentinelOne bought Observo, Sentinel added cheap data-lake tiers.
summary: Crowded, well-funded enterprise market rapidly being bundled into SIEMs. Only a thin opening: self-serve, transparently priced, low-ops log reduction for small teams or MSSPs on Sentinel/Elastic/Wazuh, likely low ACV.
